item: A kept rollup stop is counted at the long backstop as well as on an epoch move, so a delete the epoch never sees can release it
summary: The duckdb-limit stop counted the mention table only when the corpus epoch had moved; a cascade delete of a removed source or article moves neither the epoch nor a max id (serve_gate's disclosed invisible classes), so a corpus that shrank past the 5% margin stayed held for good. The count is now also taken once the rollup backstop (1 h) has passed since the stop was last looked at; the one-a-minute floor stands and a count that is not smaller by enough refreshes checked_at and keeps the base.
